title: Time and Work - Pipe and Cistern

questions.question: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 18 hours and pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 24 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, how much time (in hours) will they take to fill the empty tank?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 18 hours and pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 24 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, how much time (in hours) will they take to fill the empty tank?
questions.solution:
Total capacity = LCM (18, 24) = 72

Pipe A fill hourly by = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units

Pipe B fills hourly by = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units

The total tank will be filled in: ⇒ 72(4 + 3) ⇒ 10(2/7) hours

questions.question: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two pipes can fill a tank in x and y minutes individually, the time taken to fill the tank together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Time taken = (36 × 45) ÷ (36 + 45)

⇒ Time taken = 1620 ÷ 81

⇒ Time taken = 20 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Pipe P to fill the tank = 36 minutes

Time taken by Pipe Q to fill the tank = 45 minutes

Calculations:

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 36 and 45 = 180 units

Pipe Time (minutes) Total Work Efficiency
P 36 180 180 ÷ 36 = 5
Q 45 180 ÷ 45 = 4

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 5 + 4 = 9 units/minute

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 180 ÷ 9

⇒ Time taken = 20 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.

Additional Information

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and its work (efficiency) is always taken as positive. An outlet pipe empties the tank and its work (efficiency) is always taken as negative.

Unitary Method for Time & Work

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled in 1 hour is 1/x. If two pipes operate simultaneously, their 1 hour work is given by (1/x + 1/y).

Three Pipes Working Together

If three pipes A, B and C have efficiencies ea, eb, and ec respectively, the total time required to fill a tank is calculated as Total Capacity ÷ (ea + eb + ec).

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously. In how much time will the empty tank be filled completely ?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously. In how much time will the empty tank be filled completely ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time is taken by A to fill the tank = 12 hrs

Time is taken by B to fill the tank = 18 hrs

Concept used:

Total time = Volume/Volume filled in 1 hour

Calculation:

Volume filled by A in 1 hr = 1/12

Volume filled by B in 1 hr = 1/18

Volume filled by both A and B in 1 hr = 1/12 + 1/18

⇒ Volume filled by both A + B in 1 hr = (3 + 2)/36

⇒ Volume filled by both (A + B) in 1 hr = 5/36

Total Time to fill the tank = (Total volume of the tank)/(Volume filled by both (A + B) in 1 hr)

⇒ Total Time to fill the tank = 1/(5/36)

⇒ Total Time to fill the tank = 36/5 hr

⇒ Total Time to fill the tank = 7 hours 12 minutes

∴ The total time to the filled the empty tank is 7 hours 12 minutes.

 Alternate Method
Efficiency of A is 3

Efficiency of B is 2

Total efficiency of A & B is 3 + 2 = 5

So total time taken to fill the tank = 36/5 = 71/5 hour = 7 hour 12 minutes

questions.question: Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 14 hours and 21 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously to fill the tank. In how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 14 hours and 21 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously to fill the tank. In how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Rate of Pipe X = 1/14, Rate of Pipe Y = 1/21

Combined rate = (1/14) + (1/21) = 5/42

Time taken = 1 / (5/42) = 8 (2/5) hours

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 20 hours and tap B can fill the same tank in 30 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: Tap A can fill a tank in 20 hours and tap B can fill the same tank in 30 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total work = 60 unit

Efficiency of A = 3 unit/hrs

Efficiency of B = 2 unit/hrs

Total efficiency of A and B = 2 + 3 = 5 unit/hrs

∴ Time taken by A and B to fill the tank = 60/5 = 12 hrs

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously to fill the tank. In how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 hours and 18 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened simultaneously to fill the tank. In how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Given:

Pipe A can fill in 15 hours.

Pipe B can fill in 18 hours.

Calculation:

Tank filled by Pipe A in 1 hour

⇒ 1/15

Tank filled by Pipe B in 1 hour

⇒ 1/18

Tank filled by both Pipes in 1 hour

⇒ (1/15) + (1/18)

⇒ 11/90

Time taken By both pipes to fill the tank

⇒ 90/11

\(\Rightarrow 8\frac{2}{{11}}\;{\rm{hours}}\)

∴ Time taken by both pipes is \(8\frac{2}{{11}}\;{\bf{hours}}\).

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time (in hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time (in hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Tap A can fill the tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours

LCM of 6 and 10 is 30

Let, the tank be of 30 units

In 1 hour tap A can fill (30/6) = 5 unit of the tank

In 1 hour tap B can empty (30/10) = 3 unit of the tank

When both the taps are opened together in 1 hour tank will be fill (5 - 3) = 2 unit

∴ To fill the tank total time needs (30/2) = 15 hours

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours, tap B can fill the same tank in 8 hours and tap C can empty the same tank in 4 hours. If all three taps A, B and C are opened together, then how much time (In hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours, tap B can fill the same tank in 8 hours and tap C can empty the same tank in 4 hours. If all three taps A, B and C are opened together, then how much time (In hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Total work = 24 units (LCM of 6, 8 and 4)

Efficiency of tap A = 4 units/day

Efficiency of tap B = 3 units/day

Efficiency of tap C = -6 units/day

∴ Time taken by A, B and C to fill the tank = 24/(4 + 3 - 6) = 24 hours

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 minutes; pipe B can fill it in 18 minutes, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 36 minutes. If all the pipes are opened simultaneously, how much time will it take to fill the empty tank completely?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 minutes; pipe B can fill it in 18 minutes, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 36 minutes. If all the pipes are opened simultaneously, how much time will it take to fill the empty tank completely?
questions.solution:
Let the total capacity of the tank = 72 units [LCM of 12, 18 and 36]

Efficiency of Pipe A = 72/12 = 6

Efficiency of Pipe B = 72/18 = 4  

Efficiency of Pipe C = 72/36 = -2 (outlet pipe)  

Combined efficiency of (A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + (-2) = 8

So, Time taken by (A + B + C) to fill the tank = 72/8 = 9 minutes

questions.question: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 5 hours and emptied by pipe B in 8 hours respectively. How much time will it take for the tank to be half full?
questions.questionHtml: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 5 hours and emptied by pipe B in 8 hours respectively. How much time will it take for the tank to be half full?
questions.solution:
Pipe alone can fill the tank in = 5 hrs

Pipe alone can empty the tank in = 8 hrs

Let tank to be half full in x hrs, then

According to the question

x/5 - x/8 = 1/2

(8x - 5x)/40 = 1/2

3x/40 = 1/2

3x = (1/2) × 40 = 20

x = 20/3 = \(6\frac{2}{3}{\rm{h}}\)

questions.question: A pipe can fill an empty tank in 5 minutes and another pipe can empty it in 6 minutes. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, in how much time will the empty tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: A pipe can fill an empty tank in 5 minutes and another pipe can empty it in 6 minutes. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, in how much time will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For one pipe filling the tank in x minutes and another emptying it in y minutes (where y > x), the total time to fill the empty tank is calculated directly.

Total Time = (x × y) ÷ (y − x)

Here, x = 5 min and y = 6 min.

Total Time = (5 × 6) ÷ (6 − 5) = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 min

∴ The correct answer is 30 min.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 5 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to empty the tank = 6 minutes

Method Used:

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the tank and the individual efficiencies of the pipes.

Pipe Time (min) Total Work (LCM) Efficiency
Pipe A (Fill) 5 30 +6
Pipe B (Empty) 6 −5

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 5 and 6, which is 30 units.

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe A = 30 ÷ 5 = +6 units/min (positive work)

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe B = 30 ÷ 6 = −5 units/min (negative work)

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipe A and Pipe B when opened together = 6 − 5 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Total time required to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Total time = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 30 min.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

This topic is an extension of Time and Work. A filling pipe does positive work (+), while an emptying pipe or a leak does negative work (−).

Two Filling Pipes

If two pipes A and B fill a tank in x and y hours respectively, the combined time taken to fill the tank is (x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Leakage Effect

If a tank fills in x hours, but due to a leak it takes y hours to fill (y > x), then the leak alone can empty the completely full tank in (x × y) ÷ (y − x) hours.

questions.question: A tap can fill a cistern in 10 minutes and another tap can empty it in 12 minutes. If both the taps are open, the time (in hours) taken to fill the tank will be:
questions.questionHtml: A tap can fill a cistern in 10 minutes and another tap can empty it in 12 minutes. If both the taps are open, the time (in hours) taken to fill the tank will be:
questions.solution:
Filling rate by tap 1 = 1/10 per minute

Emptying rate by tap 2 = 1/12 per minute 

Net filling rate = 1/10 - 1/12 = 1/60 per minute

Time to fill the tank = 1/(1/60) = 1 hour.

questions.question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 60 hours while pipe Y can fill the tank in 72 hours. Both pipes are opened together for 20 hours. How much of the tank is left empty?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe X can fill a tank in 60 hours while pipe Y can fill the tank in 72 hours. Both pipes are opened together for 20 hours. How much of the tank is left empty?
questions.solution:
Part of tank filled by X in 1 hour = 1/60, Part of tank filled by Y in 1 hour = 1/72

Part of tank filled by both in 1 hour = (1/60) + (1/72) = (6/360) + (5/360) = 11/360

Part of tank filled in 20 hours = 20 × (11/360) = 220/360 = 11/18

Part of tank left empty = 1 - (11/18) = (18/18) - (11/18) = 7/18

questions.question: One fourth of a tank can be filled in 3 hours by pipe A and one-third of the same tank can be filled in 2 hours by pipe B. How long will it take for the tank to be filled if both the pipes are kept open?
questions.questionHtml: One fourth of a tank can be filled in 3 hours by pipe A and one-third of the same tank can be filled in 2 hours by pipe B. How long will it take for the tank to be filled if both the pipes are kept open?
questions.solution:
Pipe A alone can fill the full tank in = 3 × 4 = 12 hrs

A alone can fill the tank in 1 hr = 1/12 tank

Pipe B alone can fill the full tank in = 2 × 3 = 6 hr

B alone can fill the tank in 1 hr = 1/6 tank

Pipe (A + B) can fill the tank in 1 hr = (1/12 + 1/6) = (1 + 2)/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 tank

Pipe (A + B) together fill the whole tank = 4 hrs

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, opening pipe B first, in how many hours, will the empty tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 hours and 16 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each, opening pipe B first, in how many hours, will the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Given:

Pipe A fills the empty tank in 10 hours

Pipe B fills the empty tank in 16 hours

Concept Used:

Total work = LCM of time taken by each pipe

Calculation:

LCM of 16 and 10 = 80

Let total work be 80 units

Pipe A does = 80/10 = 8 units per hour

Pipe B does = 80/16 = 5 units per hour

Now,

Pipe B & A fill the tank in two hour

⇒ (5 + 8) units

⇒ 13 units

Now,

Each B & A will keep filling the tank for = (80/13) ≈ 6 hours 

After (6 × 2) = 12 hours, the tank will be filled by (13 × 6) = 78 units. 

2 units are yet to be filled

On, 13th hour B will be opened. 

It will take 2/5 hour for B to fill the remaining tank entirely.

Total time = 12 + 2/5 = \(12\frac{2}{5}\) hours 

∴ The empty tank will be filled in \(12\frac{2}{5}\) hours.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 4 hours and another pipe B is installed. Both the pipes together fill the cistern in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) hours. How long will it take for B alone to fill the cistern?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 4 hours and another pipe B is installed. Both the pipes together fill the cistern in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) hours. How long will it take for B alone to fill the cistern?
questions.solution:
Detailed Solution∶

Efficiency of pipe A = 1/4

Time taken by both the pipe to fill the cistern when they work together = 5/2 hours

Efficiency of both the pipe when they work together = 2/5

Efficiency of pipe B = 2/5 - 1/4 = 3/20

Time taken by pipe B to fill the cistern = 1/(3/20) = 20/3 hours = \(6\frac{2}{3}\) hours

Alternate Solution∶

Efficiency of B = A + B – A = 8 – 5 = 3

Time taken by B to fill the cistern = 20/3 = \(6\frac{2}{3}\)

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened together for 3 hours. After that pipe A is closed, and B continues to fill the tank. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened together for 3 hours. After that pipe A is closed, and B continues to fill the tank. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Rate of work A = 1/6, Rate of work B = 1/8

Work done by both pipes in 3 hours  = 3(1/6 + 1/8) = 3(7/24) = 7/8

Remaining work = 1 - 7/8 = 1/8, Time for B = (1/8) / (1/8) = 1 hr

Total time to fill the tank = 3 hours (both pipes) + 1 hour (pipe B) = 4 hours

questions.question: Pipe L can fill a pool in 30 hours and pipe M in 45 hours. If both the pipes are opened in an empty pool, how much time will they take to fill it?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe L can fill a pool in 30 hours and pipe M in 45 hours. If both the pipes are opened in an empty pool, how much time will they take to fill it?
questions.solution:
Work rate of Pipe L = 1/30 (pool/hour), Work rate of Pipe M = 1/45 (pool/hour)

Combined work rate = 1/30 + 1/45 = (3+2)/90 = 1/18 (pool/hour)

Time taken to fill the pool together = 1 / (1/18) = 18 hours

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank 6 times faster than another pipe. If both the pipes together can fill the tank in 40 minutes, then in how many minutes will the slower pipe alone be able to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: One pipe can fill a tank 6 times faster than another pipe. If both the pipes together can fill the tank in 40 minutes, then in how many minutes will the slower pipe alone be able to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Let the rate of the slower pipe be x tanks/min.

Faster pipe rate = 6x tanks/min

Combined rate = 7x tanks/min

7x = 1/40

x = 1/280

Time for slower pipe = 1/x = 280 minutes

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 45 minutes. If pipe A can fill an empty tank in 1 hour, how long will it take pipe B to fill the empty tank?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 45 minutes. If pipe A can fill an empty tank in 1 hour, how long will it take pipe B to fill the empty tank?
questions.solution:
As we know

1 hr = 60 min

Total work = 180

Efficiency of (A + B) = 4

Efficiency of A = 3

Efficiency of B = (A + B) – A = 4 – 3 = 1

Time taken to fill the tank by B = 180/1 = 180 min = 180/60 = 3 hr

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 6 and 8 hours respectively, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then the tank will get filled in:
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 6 and 8 hours respectively, while pipe C can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then the tank will get filled in:
questions.solution:
Total work = 120 unit

The tank will fill if all three pipes open together = 120/(20 + 15 - 12) = 120/23 = \(5\frac{5}{{23}}\;hrs\)

questions.question: Tap P can fill a cistern in 6 hours and tap Q can empty the full cistern in 10 hours. If both taps P and Q are kept open simultaneously, then in how many hours will the empty cistern be completely full ?
questions.questionHtml: Tap P can fill a cistern in 6 hours and tap Q can empty the full cistern in 10 hours. If both taps P and Q are kept open simultaneously, then in how many hours will the empty cistern be completely full ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Tap P's 1 hour's work = 1/6

Tap Q's 1 hour's work = 1/10

Calculation:

Tap(P + Q)'s 1 hour's work = 1/6 - 1/10 = 4/60 = 1/15

∴ In 15 hours tank will be full.

Shortcut Trick

  Time Work Efficiency
P 6
30
 5
Q 10 3

⇒ (P + Q)'s combined efficiency = 5 - 3 = 2units/h

⇒ Time is taken to fill tank = 30/2 = 15 h

questions.question: A tank is filled in 45 minutes by two pipes, A and B. Pipe B fills the tank twice as fast as A. How much time (in minutes) will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: A tank is filled in 45 minutes by two pipes, A and B. Pipe B fills the tank twice as fast as A. How much time (in minutes) will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Let the time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank be x minutes

Rate of filling of pipe A = 1/x

Rate of filling of pipe B = 2/x

Combined rate = 1/x + 2/x = 3/x

Given combined rate = 1/45 ⇒ 3/x = 1/45

⇒ x = 3 × 45 ⇒ x = 135 minutes

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each starting with pipe A first. In how many hours the tank will be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 hours respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 hour each starting with pipe A first. In how many hours the tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
Capacity of the tank = LCM of the time taken by A and B.

Capacity of the tank = 18 units

A’s efficiency = 18/6 = 3 units per hour

B’s efficiency = 18/9 = 2 units per hour

2 hours work for A and B = (3 + 2) = 5 units

⇒ 2 × 3 hours = 3 × 5 or 15 units

⇒ 6 hours = 15 units

⇒ 7 hours = 18 units. (At last A fills remaining 3 units)

∴ Tank will be filled in 7 hours.

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank four times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 48 minutes, the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
questions.questionHtml: One pipe can fill a tank four times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 48 minutes, the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
questions.solution:
If the faster pipe fills the tank in time t1, then the slower pipe takes t2 = 4 × t1.

⇒ (1/t1) + (1/(4t1)) = 1/48

⇒ t1 = (5×48)/4 = 60 min

⇒ t2 = 4×t1 = 4×60 = 240 min

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 4 hours and Pipe B can fill the same cistern in 5 hours. Pipe C can empty a full cistern in 3 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then the time (in minutes) taken to fill the tank is: (round to the nearest minute)
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 4 hours and Pipe B can fill the same cistern in 5 hours. Pipe C can empty a full cistern in 3 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, then the time (in minutes) taken to fill the tank is: (round to the nearest minute)
questions.solution:
Rate of filling by A = 1/4

Rate of filling by B = 1/5

Rate of emptying by C = 1/3

Net rate = 1/4 + 1/5 - 1/3 = 7/60

Time = 1 / (7/60) = 60/7 hours = 514 minutes

questions.question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 9 hours and Pipe Y can fill it in 21 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and Pipe X is opened first, in how many hours shall the tank be full?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe X can fill a tank in 9 hours and Pipe Y can fill it in 21 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and Pipe X is opened first, in how many hours shall the tank be full?
questions.solution:
In 2 hours: (1)/(9) + (1)/(21) = (7)/(63) + (3)/(63) = (10)/(63)

After t = 2n hours: (10)/(63) × n = 1 ⇒ n = 63/10 = 6.3

Total time t = 2(6.3) = 12.6 hours = 12(3/7) hours.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill 50% of the tank in 6 hours and pipe B can completely fill the same tank in 18 hours. If both the pipes are opened at the same time, in how much time (in minutes) will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A can fill 50% of the tank in 6 hours and pipe B can completely fill the same tank in 18 hours. If both the pipes are opened at the same time, in how much time (in minutes) will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Pipe A can feel the complete tank in 6 × 2 = 12 hrs

Let total work is 36 units ( LCM of 12 and 18) 

The efficiency of pipe A is 36 /12 = 3units. The efficiency of pipe B is 36 /18 = 2units

The efficiency of pipe A + B is 2 + 3 = 5 units

The time will be , 36 /5 = 7.2 hrs ⇒ 7.2 × 60 = 432 minutes

questions.question: 12 buckets of water fill a tank when the capacity of each bucket is 13.5 litres. How many buckets will be needed to fill the same tank, if the capacity of each bucket is 9 litres?
questions.questionHtml: 12 buckets of water fill a tank when the capacity of each bucket is 13.5 litres. How many buckets will be needed to fill the same tank, if the capacity of each bucket is 9 litres?
questions.solution:
Given∶ Capacity of each bucket = 13.5 litres

Number of buckets require to fill the tank = 12

Calculation∶

Total capacity of the tank = 13.5 × 12 = 162 litres

Number of bucket required to fill the tank if capacity of bucket is 9 litres = Total capacity of the tank/capacity of each bucket = 162/9 = 18

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened together when a tank is empty, in how many hours will 35% tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 9 respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened together when a tank is empty, in how many hours will 35% tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the capacity of tank be 36 units

The efficiency of A = 6 unit per hr

The efficiency of B = 4 unit per hr

Efficiency of C = -3 unit per hr

35% of tank capacity = 36 × 35/100 = 12.6

Combined efficiency = 6 + 4 - 3 = 7

∴ Required time = 12.6 ÷ 7 = 1.8 h

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill a water storage tank in 11 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 15 hours. If both pipes opened simultaneously. The time taken to fill the empty tank (in hrs) is :
questions.questionHtml: An inlet pipe can fill a water storage tank in 11 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 15 hours. If both pipes opened simultaneously. The time taken to fill the empty tank (in hrs) is :
questions.solution:
Inlet rate = 1/11, Outlet rate = 1/15

⇒ Net rate = (1/11) - (1/15) = (15/165) - (11/165) = 4/165

⇒ Time = 1 / (4/165) = 41 (1/4) hrs

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
If a pipe can fill or empty in A hours, then it can fill or empty 1/A part in 1 hour.

Together they can fill  in 1 hour = 1/16 + 1/24 – 1/40 part = 19/240

Together they can fill 190/240 = 19/24 part in 10 hours

Remaining tank = 1 – 19/24 = 5/24

B and C can do 1/24 – 1/40 = 2/120 = 1/60

B and C can fill a tank in 60 hours

B and C can fill 5/24 tank in 60 × 5/24 = 25/2 = \(12 \dfrac{1}{2}\) hours

questions.question: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 8:00 a.m., pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 9:00 a.m.?
questions.questionHtml: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 4 hours and pipe B in 6 hours. At 8:00 a.m., pipe A was opened. At what time will the tank be filled if pipe B is opened at 9:00 a.m.?
questions.solution:
Work done by A in 1 hour = 1/4

Combined work done by A and B in 1 hour = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12

Remaining work after 9:00 a.m. = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4

Time to complete remaining work = (3/4) / (5/12) = 9/5 hours = 1.8 hours

1.8 hours = 1 hour and 48 minutes

Tank will be filled at 9:00 a.m. + 1 hour 48 minutes = 10:48 a.m.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 3 hours. In how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 12 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 3 hours. In how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Pipe A can alone fill a tank in = 6 hrs

Pipe B alone can fill a tank in = 8 hrs

Pipe C alone can fill a tank in = 12 hrs

Let B and C together fill the remaining tank in x hrs

According to the question

\(\Rightarrow \frac{3}{6}{\rm{\;}} + \frac{{\left( {3{\rm{\;}} + {\rm{\;x}}} \right)}}{8} - \frac{{\left( {3{\rm{\;}} + {\rm{\;x}}} \right)}}{{12}} = 1\)

⇒ (1/2) + [3(3 + x) - 2(3 + x)]/24 = 1

⇒ (9 + 3x - 6 - 2x)/24 = 1 - 1/2

⇒ (x + 3)/24 = 1/2

⇒ x + 3 = 24/2 = 12

⇒ x = 12 - 3 = 9 hrs

Short Trick∶

Let pipe B and C will work x hrs after working 3 hrs.

According to the question

(4 + 3 - 2) × 3 + (3 - 2) × x = 24

15 + x = 24

x = 9 hrs

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 20 hours respectively. They are opened alternatively for 1 hour each. Starting with pipe A first. In how many hours with the empty tank be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 20 hours respectively. They are opened alternatively for 1 hour each. Starting with pipe A first. In how many hours with the empty tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work (LCM of 16, 20) = 80 units.

Efficiency: A = 5, B = 4. 2-hour cycle (A+B) = 9 units.

8 cycles (16 hours) = 9 × 8 = 72 units. Remaining = 80 − 72 = 8 units.

17th hour (Pipe A) fills 5 units. Remaining = 3 units.

Time for B to finish = 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 hours. Total time = 17 + 3/4 = 17(3/4) hours.

∴ The correct answer is 17(3/4) hours.

Alternate Method

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Pipe A 16 hours 80 units 5
Pipe B 20 hours 4

Calculation:

⇒ Total capacity of tank = LCM(16, 20) = 80 units.

⇒ Work done in 1st hour (A) = 5 units.

⇒ Work done in 2nd hour (B) = 4 units.

⇒ Work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 5 + 4 = 9 units.

⇒ In 8 cycles (16 hours), work done = 9 × 8 = 72 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 80 − 72 = 8 units.

⇒ On 17th hour, Pipe A works and fills 5 units.

⇒ Remaining work after 17 hours = 8 − 5 = 3 units.

⇒ Now it is Pipe B's turn. Time taken by B = 3/4 hours.

⇒ Total time = 17 + 3/4 = 17(3/4) hours.

∴ The correct answer is 17(3/4) hours.

Additional Information

Alternate Work Principle

When pipes work alternatively, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (sum of individual efficiencies) and multiply to reach near the total work.

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time. For inlet pipes, efficiency is positive; for outlet pipes, it is negative.

questions.question: Pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 18 and 27 minutes, respectively, whereas pipe R can empty the full tank in 54 minutes. P and Q were opened together for 6 minutes and then closed and R was opened. The tank was emptied by R alone in:
questions.questionHtml: Pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 18 and 27 minutes, respectively, whereas pipe R can empty the full tank in 54 minutes. P and Q were opened together for 6 minutes and then closed and R was opened. The tank was emptied by R alone in:
questions.solution:
Given:

Pipe P filling time = 18 minutes

Pipe Q filling time = 27 minutes

Pipe R empty time = 54 minutes

P and Q opened for 6 minutes

Formula used:

Capacity = time × efficiency

Calculation:

Total work = 54 unit

Work done by pipe P and Q in 6 min = (3 + 2) × 6 = 30

Pipe R empty the tank in = 30/1 = 30 min

∴ The correct answer is 30 min.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Due to leakage in the bottom it is filled in 20 hours. If the tank is full, and the pipe is closed, how much time will the leak take to empty the entire tank?
questions.questionHtml: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Due to leakage in the bottom it is filled in 20 hours. If the tank is full, and the pipe is closed, how much time will the leak take to empty the entire tank?
questions.solution:
Efficiency Pipe Time Total capacity
4 P 15 60
3 P + L 20

So, Efficiency of the leakage = (4 - 3) = 1 unit/hr

Time taken to empty the tank = 60/1 = 60 hrs

questions.question: Pipe A and B can empty a full tank in 18 hours and 24 hours, respectively. Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 36 hours. If the tank is 5/6 full and all the three pipes are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be emptied?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A and B can empty a full tank in 18 hours and 24 hours, respectively. Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 36 hours. If the tank is 5/6 full and all the three pipes are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be emptied?
questions.solution:
Given:

Pipe A and B can empty a full tank in 18 hours and 24 hours.

Pipe C alone can fill the tank in 36 hours.

The tank is 5/6 full and all the three pipes are opened together.

Concept used:

Time required = Total work/Efficiency

Calculation:

Total work = 72

5/6 of total work = 72 × 5/6 = 60

If all three pipe open together then, 5/6 of the tank empty in = 60/(-4 -3 + 2) = 60/-5 = 12 hrs

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 72 and 90 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are left open how long will it take for the cistern to be half full?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 72 and 90 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are left open how long will it take for the cistern to be half full?
questions.solution:
Detailed Solution∶

Efficiency of 1st pipe = 1/72

Efficiency of 2nd pipe = 1/90

Total efficiency = (1/72) + (1/90) = 1/40

Time taken by both the pipes to fill the cistern half full = (1/2) / (1/40) = 20 minutes

Alternate Solution∶

Capacity of half-filled cistern = 1/2 × 360 = 180

Time taken by both pipes to fill half cistern = 180/(5 + 4) = 20 minutes

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 30 hours. Due to a leakage at the bottom, it is filled in 50 hours. How much time will the leakage take to empty the completely filled tank?
questions.questionHtml: A pipe can fill a tank in 30 hours. Due to a leakage at the bottom, it is filled in 50 hours. How much time will the leakage take to empty the completely filled tank?
questions.solution: Time taken to empty the completely filled tank = [(50) × 30] /(50 - 30) = (1500)/(20) = 75 hours

questions.question: Three pipes X, Y and Z discharge three different chemicals A, B and C in a tank. The pipes can fill the tank in 20, 25 and 40 minutes respectively. What will be the proportion of chemical B in the tank, if all the pipes are open for 10 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: Three pipes X, Y and Z discharge three different chemicals A, B and C in a tank. The pipes can fill the tank in 20, 25 and 40 minutes respectively. What will be the proportion of chemical B in the tank, if all the pipes are open for 10 minutes?
questions.solution:
From the following figure

Pipe X alone can fill the tank in 1 min = 10

Pipe X alone can fill the tank in 10 min = 10 × 10 = 100

Pipe Y alone can fill the tank in 1 min = 8

Pipe Y alone can fill the tank in 10 min = 8 × 10 = 80

Pipe Z alone can fill the tank in 1 min = 5

Pipe Z alone can fill the tank in 10 min = 5 × 10 = 50

Proportion of chemical B after 10 min = 80/(100 + 80 + 50) = 80/230 = 8/23

questions.question: Pipe A usually fills a tank in 6 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom of the tank, it takes extra 2 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, then how much time will it take to get emptied due to the leak?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A usually fills a tank in 6 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom of the tank, it takes extra 2 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, then how much time will it take to get emptied due to the leak?
questions.solution:
Work rate of the leak = (1 / 6) - (1 / 8)

= (4 - 3) / 24 = 1 / 24 (tank/hour)

Time to empty the tank = 1 / (1 / 24) = 24 hours

questions.question: Two pipes S1 and S2 alone can fill an empty tank in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively. Pipe S3 alone can empty that completely filled tank in 40 hours. Firstly both pipes S1 and S2 are opened and after 2 hour pipe S3 is also opened. In how much time tank will be completely filled after S3 is opened?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes S1 and S2 alone can fill an empty tank in 15 hours and 20 hours respectively. Pipe S3 alone can empty that completely filled tank in 40 hours. Firstly both pipes S1 and S2 are opened and after 2 hour pipe S3 is also opened. In how much time tank will be completely filled after S3 is opened?
questions.solution:
Let total work is 120 units ( LCM of 15 , 20 and 40) 

The efficiency of pipe s1 is 120 /15 = 8 units . The efficiency of pipe s2 is 120 / 20  = 6 units

The efficiency of pipe S1 + S2 is  8 + 6= 14 units. In 2 hrs they will fill 14 × 2 = 28 units

Remaining amount 120 - 28 = 92 units. The efficiency of pipe s3 is 120 / 40  = - 3 units

Now combined efficiency of all three pipes is 14 - 3 = 11 units

Time to fill remaining 92 units is , 92 / 11 hr

questions.question: Two inlet pipes, P1 and P2, can fill a cistern in 20 hours and 30 hours, respectively. They were opened at the same time, but pipe P1 had to be closed 5 hours before the cistern was full. How many hours in total did it take for the two pipes to fill the cistern?
questions.questionHtml: Two inlet pipes, P1 and P2, can fill a cistern in 20 hours and 30 hours, respectively. They were opened at the same time, but pipe P1 had to be closed 5 hours before the cistern was full. How many hours in total did it take for the two pipes to fill the cistern?
questions.solution:
Rate of P1 = 1/20, Rate of P2 = 1/30

⇒ (t - 5)/20 + t/30 = 1 ⇒ (3(t - 5) + 2t)/60 = 1 ⇒ (5t - 15)/60 = 1

⇒ 5t - 15 = 60 ⇒ t = 15 hours.

questions.question: Pipes P and Q can completely fill a water tank in 10 hours and 15 hours, respectively. A pipe R can empty a tank filled completely with water in 12 hours. Initially, the tank is empty and only pipes P and Q are opened at 6 a.m. and pipe R is also opened at 9 a.m. By what time will the tank be completely filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes P and Q can completely fill a water tank in 10 hours and 15 hours, respectively. A pipe R can empty a tank filled completely with water in 12 hours. Initially, the tank is empty and only pipes P and Q are opened at 6 a.m. and pipe R is also opened at 9 a.m. By what time will the tank be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Work rate of P = 1/10, Work rate of Q = 1/15, Work rate of R = 1/12

From 6 a.m. to 9 a.m.: Work done = (1/10 + 1/15) × 3 = 1/2

After 9 a.m.: Net work rate = 1/10 + 1/15 - 1/12 = 1/12

Time required = (1/2) / (1/12) = 6 hours

9 a.m. + 6 hours = 3 p.m.

questions.question: Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 18 minutes, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 18 minutes, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe C is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled ?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours, respectively, whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe C is closed after 10 hours. After how many hours will the remaining part of the tank be filled ?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Pipe A, B, and C can fill in 1 hour

⇒ 15 + 10 - 6

⇒ 19

(A + B + C) can fill in 10 hours

⇒ 19 × 10

⇒ 190

Remaining empty tank

⇒ 240 - 190

⇒ 50

Remaining empty tank filled by A and B

⇒ 50/25

⇒ 2 hours

∴ Time taken to fill remaining tank is 2 hours.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 8 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 8 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.solution:
Part filled by 1st pipe in 1 hour = 1/12

Part filled by 2nd pipe in 1 hour = 1/18

Part emptied by 3rd pipe in 1 hour = 1/8

Net part filled in 1 hour = (1/12) + (1/18) - (1/8)

LCM of 12, 18, and 8 = 72

1/12 = 6/72, 1/18 = 4/72, 1/8 = 9/72

Net part filled = (6 + 4 - 9)/72 = 1/72

Time = 1 / (1/72) = 72 hours

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours respectively whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 8 hours. After how many hours, the remaining part of tank will be filled?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours respectively whereas pipe C can empty the full tank in 40 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 8 hours. After how many hours, the remaining part of tank will be filled?
questions.solution:
Pipe A can alone fill the tank in = 16 hrs

Pipe B alone can fill the tank in = 24 hrs

Pipe C alone can empty the tank in = 40 hrs

Let B and C together fill the remaining tank in x hrs

According to the question

\(\Rightarrow \frac{8}{{16}} + \frac{{\left( {8 + {\rm{x}}} \right)}}{{24}} - \frac{{\left( {8 + {\rm{x}}} \right)}}{{40}} = 1\)

⇒ (1/2) + [5(8 + x) - 3(8 + x)]/120 = 1

⇒ (40 + 5x - 24 - 3x)/120 = 1 - 1/2

⇒ (2x + 16)/120 = 1/2

⇒ 2x + 16 = 120/2 = 60

⇒ 2x = 60 - 16 = 44 hrs

⇒ x = 44/2 = 22 hrs

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in \(1\frac{1}{3}\) hours and 2 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in \(1\frac{1}{3}\) hours and 2 hours, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
Rate of A = 1 / (4/3) = 3/4 tank/hr

Rate of B = 1 / 2 = 1/2 tank/hr

Combined rate = (3/4) + (1/2) = (3/4) + (2/4) = 5/4 tank/hr

Time to fill = 1 / (5/4) = 4/5 hrs = 48 mins
